stock.name: Royal Bank of Canada
stock.blurb: Royal Bank is Canada's biggest bank. It makes money from everyday accounts, loans, and looking after investments.

stock.name: Toronto-Dominion Bank
stock.blurb: TD serves millions of people in Canada and the United States through branches, cards, and loans.

stock.name: Bank of Nova Scotia
stock.blurb: Scotiabank is a Canadian bank with a large presence in Latin America as well as at home.

stock.name: Bank of Montreal
stock.blurb: BMO is a major Canadian bank. Personal banking and business lending are the core of the story.

stock.name: Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce
stock.blurb: CIBC is a Canadian bank focused on personal banking, business loans, and wealth management.

stock.name: National Bank of Canada
stock.blurb: National Bank is based in Montreal and is strongest in Quebec, with a growing business across Canada.

stock.name: Manulife Financial
stock.blurb: Manulife sells life insurance and retirement products in Canada, the United States, and Asia.

stock.name: Sun Life Financial
stock.blurb: Sun Life sells insurance and manages retirement savings, including plans people get through work.

stock.name: Great-West Lifeco
stock.blurb: Great-West Lifeco owns insurance brands in Canada, the United States, and Europe.

stock.name: Intact Financial
stock.blurb: Intact is Canada's largest home and car insurer. Customers pay premiums, and Intact pays claims.

stock.name: iA Financial
stock.blurb: iA Financial sells insurance and wealth products, with deep roots in Quebec.

stock.name: Brookfield Corporation
stock.blurb: Brookfield Corporation owns pieces of real estate, power, and infrastructure around the world.

stock.name: Brookfield Asset Management
stock.blurb: Brookfield Asset Management runs money for large clients and earns fees for doing it.

stock.name: Fairfax Financial
stock.blurb: Fairfax is an insurance group that also invests the premium money, a bit like a Canadian Berkshire.

stock.name: Power Corporation of Canada
stock.blurb: Power Corporation is a holding company. It owns stakes in insurers and wealth businesses.

stock.name: Shopify
stock.blurb: Shopify sells the software that lets a shop run online, from the product page to the checkout.

stock.name: Constellation Software
stock.blurb: Constellation buys small software companies that other businesses quietly rely on, then holds them.

stock.name: Thomson Reuters
stock.blurb: Thomson Reuters sells information and software to lawyers, accountants, and newsrooms.

stock.name: Open Text
stock.blurb: Open Text sells software that large organizations use to store and manage documents.

stock.name: CGI
stock.blurb: CGI is an IT firm. Governments and companies hire it to build and run computer systems.

stock.name: Enbridge
stock.blurb: Enbridge moves oil and natural gas through pipelines, and it also owns gas utilities.

stock.name: TC Energy
stock.blurb: TC Energy runs pipelines that carry natural gas across North America.

stock.name: Canadian Natural Resources
stock.blurb: Canadian Natural Resources produces oil and gas, much of it from Alberta.

stock.name: Suncor Energy
stock.blurb: Suncor produces oil from the oil sands and sells fuel through Petro-Canada stations.

stock.name: Imperial Oil
stock.blurb: Imperial Oil produces oil and sells fuel. ExxonMobil owns a majority of the company.

stock.name: Cenovus Energy
stock.blurb: Cenovus produces oil, including from the oil sands, and refines it into fuel.

stock.name: Pembina Pipeline
stock.blurb: Pembina moves and stores oil and gas through pipelines and processing plants.

stock.name: Tourmaline Oil
stock.blurb: Tourmaline is one of Canada's biggest natural gas producers.

stock.name: Canadian National Railway
stock.blurb: Canadian National runs a railway from the Atlantic to the Pacific and down into the United States.

stock.name: Canadian Pacific Kansas City
stock.blurb: This railway links Canada, the United States, and Mexico, hauling freight across the continent.

stock.name: Waste Connections
stock.blurb: Waste Connections collects garbage and recycling, mostly in smaller cities.

stock.name: WSP Global
stock.blurb: WSP is an engineering firm. It designs roads, buildings, and transit systems.

stock.name: TFI International
stock.blurb: TFI is a trucking company. It hauls freight across North America.

stock.name: Stantec
stock.blurb: Stantec designs buildings, water systems, and other infrastructure projects.

stock.name: CAE
stock.blurb: CAE builds flight simulators and trains pilots for airlines and defence customers.

stock.name: Alimentation Couche-Tard
stock.blurb: Couche-Tard runs convenience stores, including Circle K, in many countries.

stock.name: Dollarama
stock.blurb: Dollarama sells low-priced household goods from a huge chain of Canadian stores.

stock.name: Loblaw
stock.blurb: Loblaw runs grocery stores such as Loblaws, No Frills, and Real Canadian Superstore.

stock.name: Metro
stock.blurb: Metro runs grocery stores, mostly in Quebec and Ontario.

stock.name: Empire Company
stock.blurb: Empire owns Sobeys, Safeway, and other grocery banners.

stock.name: Restaurant Brands
stock.blurb: Restaurant Brands owns Tim Hortons, Burger King, and Popeyes.

stock.name: Magna International
stock.blurb: Magna builds parts and systems for car makers around the world.

stock.name: Canadian Tire
stock.blurb: Canadian Tire sells tools, sports gear, and home goods, and it also owns a bank and clothing banners.

stock.name: Barrick Mining
stock.blurb: Barrick is a global gold miner, with mines in several countries.

stock.name: Agnico Eagle Mines
stock.blurb: Agnico Eagle mines gold, including large mines in Canada.

stock.name: Nutrien
stock.blurb: Nutrien sells fertilizer — potash, nitrogen, and phosphate — to farms.

stock.name: Franco-Nevada
stock.blurb: Franco-Nevada does not run mines. It buys a slice of what other mines produce.

stock.name: Wheaton Precious Metals
stock.blurb: Wheaton funds mines in exchange for a share of their silver and gold.

stock.name: Teck Resources
stock.blurb: Teck is a miner best known now for copper and zinc.

stock.name: Cameco
stock.blurb: Cameco mines uranium, the fuel used in nuclear power plants.

stock.name: BCE
stock.blurb: BCE owns Bell. It sells phone, internet, and TV service, and it has media brands too.

stock.name: TELUS
stock.blurb: TELUS sells wireless and internet service, and it also has a health-software business.

stock.name: Rogers Communications
stock.blurb: Rogers sells wireless, internet, and cable, and it owns sports media.

stock.name: Quebecor
stock.blurb: Quebecor owns Videotron, a major phone and internet provider in Quebec.

stock.name: Fortis
stock.blurb: Fortis owns electric and gas utilities in Canada, the United States, and the Caribbean.

stock.name: Emera
stock.blurb: Emera owns power utilities, including Nova Scotia Power and some businesses in the United States.

stock.name: Hydro One
stock.blurb: Hydro One runs much of the electricity transmission network across Ontario.

stock.name: Algonquin Power & Utilities
stock.blurb: Algonquin owns power and water utilities. Its dividend has been a bumpy story, which is part of the lesson.

stock.name: Brookfield Renewable
stock.blurb: Brookfield Renewable owns hydro, wind, and solar plants.

stock.name: Brookfield Infrastructure
stock.blurb: Brookfield Infrastructure owns assets such as toll roads, data centers, and utilities.
